content.value_statement: Complex GraphQL systems can become slow, inconsistent, and hard to govern. This skill guides schema design, federation planning, caching, security, and operations.
actual_capabilities: Plans federated GraphQL architecture with subgraphs, gateways, and schema governance.
Designs schemas with interfaces, unions, connections, custom scalars, and versioning guidance.
Recommends performance controls such as DataLoader, query complexity limits, APQ, and caching.
Maps security requirements to field authorization, JWT validation, RBAC, rate limits, and production hardening.
Designs real-time GraphQL subscriptions with authorization, filtering, and scalable delivery patterns.
Outlines testing, observability, load testing, and schema change validation practices.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance but does not run GraphQL servers or benchmark live APIs.
It needs project schema, traffic, team, and infrastructure details for precise recommendations.
It cannot verify third-party service behavior without current project documentation.
It does not replace security review for production authorization and data exposure rules.

use_cases.title: Plan a federated platform
use_cases.description: Design service boundaries, subgraph ownership, schema governance, and gateway rollout steps.

use_cases.title: Fix GraphQL performance issues
use_cases.description: Identify N+1 risks, caching opportunities, query limits, and monitoring needs for a slow API.

use_cases.title: Harden a production schema
use_cases.description: Review authorization, rate limits, introspection policy, input validation, and subscription controls.

prompt_templates.title: Review my schema direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my GraphQL schema goals and suggest a simple production-ready design. Focus on types, relationships, validation, and future changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a federation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GraphQL federation plan for these teams and services. Include subgraph boundaries, ownership, schema governance, and rollout risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize API performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this GraphQL API for performance risks. Recommend resolver batching, caching, query limits, monitoring, and load testing priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Create an enterprise migration strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a REST-to-GraphQL migration strategy for an enterprise platform. Include compatibility, federation, security, subscriptions, observability, and phased delivery.

output_examples.input: Design a GraphQL architecture for a marketplace with catalog, orders, users, and payments.
output: A proposed federated architecture with separate catalog, order, identity, and payment subgraphs.
Guidance for entity ownership, gateway composition, schema review, and staged rollout.
Security and observability checkpoints for authorization, tracing, rate limits, and schema changes.

output_examples.input: Our GraphQL API has slow product pages and many repeated database calls.
output: A performance review that targets resolver batching, DataLoader placement, query depth controls, and cache boundaries.
Recommendations for persisted queries, field-level cache policy, tracing, and benchmark scenarios.
A prioritized action list separating quick fixes from deeper schema or resolver redesign.

output_examples.input: Prepare a production hardening checklist for GraphQL subscriptions.
output: A checklist covering connection authentication, per-event authorization, filtering, rate limits, and backpressure.
Operational guidance for WebSocket scaling, monitoring, reconnection behavior, and incident response.
Testing areas for permission leaks, fan-out load, stale subscriptions, and failure recovery.

best_practices: Provide schema samples, traffic patterns, ownership boundaries, and deployment constraints before requesting architecture advice.
Ask for tradeoffs between schema simplicity, client flexibility, performance, and governance.
Validate recommendations with tests for authorization, breaking changes, query cost, and resolver performance.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a universal schema without explaining product domains and client needs.
Do not treat federation as required when a modular monolith or simple schema fits better.
Do not copy security advice into production without reviewing data exposure and business rules.

faq.question: What kind of GraphQL work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports schema design, federation, performance optimization, security planning, subscriptions, testing, and operational readiness.

faq.question: Can it generate production implementation code?
faq.answer: It can outline implementation approaches and examples, but teams should adapt and test code in their own stack.

faq.question: Does it focus only on Apollo Federation?
faq.answer: No. It covers Apollo Federation, GraphQL Fusion concepts, schema composition, gateways, and other modern GraphQL tools.

faq.question: What inputs improve the recommendations?
faq.answer: Share current schema details, service boundaries, traffic volume, client needs, security requirements, and deployment constraints.

faq.question: Can it help with GraphQL security?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan authorization, query cost controls, rate limiting, JWT validation, introspection policy, and input validation.

faq.question: Is it useful for REST-to-GraphQL migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design phased migration plans that preserve compatibility while introducing GraphQL schemas and governance.
